title: Design System: From Molecule to Machine

display.purpose: Default page and lesson h1, not the course opener's local display treatment.

headline.purpose: General h2; original-lesson headings have the reading-specific adjustments documented in DESIGN.md.

title.purpose: General h3 below the section heading.

ui.purpose: Interface surroundings, supplemental explanations, and default native fields.

body.purpose: Sustained serif reading within the constrained original-text column.

button.purpose: Stronger sans-serif labels on primary and secondary actions.

curriculum.purpose: Compact multi-line lesson navigation, strengthened for the current page.

code.purpose: System monospace in a separately scrollable code surface; inline code scales with prose.

shadows.name: dialog-lift
shadows.purpose: Modal utility separation; the source backdrop is rgb(9 23 41 / 48%).

shadows.name: storage-notice-lift
shadows.purpose: Local-storage status notice, fixed on wide screens and in flow on mobile.

motion.name: button-background
motion.purpose: Primary and secondary button background changes without movement or scale.

motion.name: reduced-motion-duration
motion.purpose: Reduced-motion animation and transition duration override; scrolling returns to auto.

components.name: Illustrative model panel
components.description: The static, non-calculating state of the active-space model from src\components\MiniLab.astro, preserving its assumption notice and disabled update action.
components.html:
Explore an active space

Interactive model

Illustrative model, not a scientific calculation. Counts only: M spatial orbitals give 2M spin modes and 2M qubits under an untapered direct occupation mapping. Fixed N alpha minus N beta is a spin projection, not proof of a total-spin eigenstate. No basis-quality or energy calculation is performed.

Enable JavaScript to explore this model. The assumptions and original lesson remain readable without it.

narrative.overview:
Cool paper, cobalt linework, and ink-blue type give technical material a calm, precise setting. Locally packaged sans and serif families distinguish orientation from sustained reading. Numbered vector plates explain relationships; native controls invite inspection without competing with the lesson.

Thin rules and restrained tonal differences organize the interface instead of stacks of elevated cards. Original source text and supplementary learning have visible labels and separate typographic treatments. This records the implemented, user-approved world, not a proposed redesign.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper surfaces with role-specific light and dark palettes.
Sans-serif orientation around a generous serif reading column.
Numbered vector plates with captions, keys, and contained horizontal scrolling.
Flat, ruled panels and native controls with explicit states.
Persistent wide-screen navigation that becomes dialogs on narrower screens.

rules.name: The Color Carries a Role Rule
rules.body: Keep navigation and explanatory structure in the accent family; reserve good and warning pairs for labeled states, and focus for keyboard position.

rules.name: The Two Reading Voices Rule
rules.body: Use sans-serif for navigation, headings, labels, and tables; serif for original narrative; monospace for code and symbolic data. Do not style supplemental model text as if it were original source prose.

rules.name: The Flat Reading, Floating Utilities Rule
rules.body: Keep lesson content, plates, and models flat and ruled. Use the existing shadow vocabulary for dialogs and storage notices, not for hover-lifting reading surfaces.

dos: Do use the complete light or dark role palette consistently across text, controls, and diagrams.
Do preserve the serif reading measure and sans-serif orientation hierarchy.
Do keep original lessons, concept explanations, and supplementary models visibly distinguished.
Do keep wide technical artifacts in labeled, keyboard-focusable scroll regions.
Do retain native controls, visible focus, explicit disabled/error states, and textual check feedback.
Do use rules and paper tones for content grouping, reserving shadows for floating utilities.
donts: Don't interchange navigation cobalt, comparison plum, confirmation green, and revisit amber.
Don't turn generated sidecar swatch ramps into new application palette tokens.
Don't make one-off opener widths or SVG coordinates into global spacing or typography rules.
Don't replace captions, source labels, or model assumptions with decorative color alone.
Don't collapse reading completion, answer selection, and correctness into one visual state.
